question.leadin: As much as 70% of the male population of this country may have been killed in the disastrous War of the Triple Alliance.
question.text: Name this country which was led by Francisco Solano Lopez from 1862 until he was killed in action in 1870.
question.clue: This country's independence is sometimes traced to Pedro Caballero's demand for the resignation of Bernardo de Velasco.

swap.text: This country consists of more than 3,000 islands and was the site of Columbus' first landfall in the New World.
swap.clue: After his abdication, Edward VIII was made governor of this country.

question.leadin: In a 19th century civil war in this country, Fructuoso Rivera's Colorados fought Manuel Oribe's agrarian Blancos.
question.text: Name this South American country where wealthy businessmen in Montevideo [mon-tay-vih-DAY-oh] supported the Colorados, the eventual winning side.
question.clue: The Italian Legion was raised in this country by the "Hero of Two Worlds," who fought in this country's civil war with the Colorados against the Blancos.

swap.leadin: Although President, this man let Valentin Gomez Farias focus on the governing of his nation.
swap.text: Name this one-legged general who ordered the Goliad Massacre and defeated Texan forces under William Travis at the Alamo.
swap.clue: While fighting a French blockade of his country's ports in the Pastry War, this leader gave a military burial to his amputated leg.

question.leadin: Name these politicians who escaped assassination.
question.text: This Cuban dictator infamously eluded many CIA plots to kill him, including one involving an exploding cigar.
question.clue: While in Mexico, he organized fellow exiles into the 26th of July movement.

swap.text: Peron's wife Isabel took power after his death in 1976, but she was soon ousted by an army coup which placed this man in power. He committed numerous human rights abuses, and the Madres de la Plaza de Mayo protest the disappearance of their children under his regime.
swap.clue: Playwright Eduardo Pavlovsky fled to Spain after this man came to power.

question.leadin: The control of this country's First Republic by two wealthy states led to it being nicknamed for their main products, "coffee and milk."
question.text: Name this country, where that republic was founded by disciples of the positivist sociologist Auguste Comte. This country was later ruled by the populist dictator Getulio Vargas.
question.answerHtml: Brazil [or Federative Republic of Brazil; accept First Brazilian Republic; accept Republic of the United States of Brazil; prompt on Old Republic]
question.clue: The Constitutionalist Revolution in this country, which demanded one ruler's power be checked, was also known as the Paulista War which, like the Pernambuco Revolt, was named for one of this country's states.

swap.leadin: While staying on this island, one leader was warned of an attempted assassination by Jose Antonio Paez.
swap.text: Name this island which titles an 1815 "Letter" advocating for Latin American unity. Earlier, this island was the site of Maroon revolts led by Nanny and Cudjoe.
swap.clue: Cudjoe and Nanny led escaped slaves on this island in fighting Europeans.

question.leadin: During his first presidential campaign, this man mocked US Ambassador Spruille Braden's "Blue Book" by publishing his own "Blue and White Book."
question.text: Name this president who served three terms from 1946 to 1974. Several of his supporters were killed by snipers in the Ezeiza massacre.
question.clue: This politician's left-wing supporters were killed at an airport in the Ezeiza (ayz-ay-EE-zah) massacre.

swap.leadin: Name the countries governed by these current presidents.
swap.text: In May 2005, its populist president Hugo Chavez demanded the extradition to this Cuban ally of a man accused of bombing a Cuban passenger airplane in 1976.
swap.answerHtml: Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela [or Republica Bolivariana de Venezuela]
swap.clue: Romulo Betancourt and Romulo Gallegos were presidents from the Democratic Action Party in this birthplace of Simon Bolivar.

question.text: The Tontons Macoute was the secret police arm of this the father and son rulers of this surname, nicknamed Papa Doc and Baby Doc.
question.clue: The second and final national leader of this surname was ousted in 1986; the first such leader created the Tonton Macoute police force.

swap.leadin: Name some key players in the Mexican Revolution.
swap.text: This president of Mexico was the recipient of the Zimmermann Telegram. This man, who gathered a commission to draft the Constitution of 1917, overthrew Victoriano Huerta with the help of Pancho Villa and Emiliano Zapata.
swap.clue: He successfully maintained World War I neutrality, but he frustrated the United States by opposing Pershing's incursion.

question.text: This man led troops in support of Juan Bautista Sacasa. Upon the intervention of US Marines, he fled to the mountains to lead a guerilla campaign. He gave his name to a later armed movement opposed by the Contras.
question.clue: This man took up arms to support the presidential claim of Juan Bautista Sacasa and successfully evaded US Marine efforts to capture him.

swap.text: This Mexican revolutionary and promulgator of the Plan of Ayala was a proponent of the ejido system.
swap.clue: This leader of the Liberation Army of the South proposed the Plan of Ayala, which was rejected by Venustiano Carranza's Constitutionalists.

question.leadin: While he was a member of a guerrilla organisation, this politician adopted the name Aureliano in homage to a Colonel in One Hundred Years of Solitude.
question.text: Elected in 2022, this politician is the first leftwing President in his country's history, and his vice-president Francia Marquez is the first black woman to hold the post.

swap.text: The Mexican independence movement began with the "Grito de Dolores," issued by this priest in 1810.
swap.clue: During an 1810 Mass, this man denounced the new Spanish monarchy in the Grito de Dolores.

question.leadin: This man's landmark book was inspired by Paul Gauthier's tract "The Poor, Jesus, and the Church."
question.text: Name this Dominican priest from Peru who became the father of liberation theology after writing the 1971 book A Theology of Liberation. He coined the notion of "God's preferential option for the poor" in his speeches, and wrote We Drink from Our Own Wells.
question.clue: Many Latin American Jesuits identified "men for others" with the preferential option for the poor, a doctrine espoused by this founder of liberation theology in On the Side of the Poor and We Drink from the Wells.

swap.text: This "Centaur of the Plains" was Bolivar's chief subordinate at the Battle of Carabobo, and drove the Spanish out of their last Venezuelan stronghold, at Puerto Cabello. He later led the independence movement of Venezuela from Gran Colombia, became its first president, and then turned dictatorial.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about a ruler whose control of the Dominican Republic was known as the "Platano Curtain."
question.text: This man was elected president in 1930 when a rebellion toppled Horacio Vasquez's government. He later banned all other political parties, renamed Santo Domingo, the province of San Cristobal, and the country's highest mountain after himself. He also oppressed Haitians in his country.
question.clue: He also ordered the killings of the Mirabal Sisters, and the failure of general Pupo Roman to act following this man's death allowed Johnny Abbes Garcia to catch and punish most of his assassins.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the short-lived First Spanish Republic.
swap.text: The brief time of the Republic also had the Spanish government continue fighting the Ten Years' War in Cuba, which more or less started when planter Carlos Manuel de Cespedes began a revolt in October 1868, an event given this name and marked by a namesake Cuban holiday.
swap.answerHtml: Grito de Yara [accept Cry of the Yara or obvious synonyms for “cry”]
